interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) diagnosis with pathological stage pT3b. Adverse findings include positive surgical margins and invasion of the seminal vesicles, as documented in the surgical pathology report. A reassuring finding is the absence of lymphovascular invasion. Nodal status is documented as "no lymph nodes were removed," which means pNx does not establish node-negative disease, widening uncertainty regarding nodal involvement. The biopsy identified Acinar adenocarcinoma. The preoperative PSA was 7. The documented findings of positive margins and seminal vesicle invasion are adverse prognostic factors. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. Missing nodal sampling further limits the staging certainty. The fixed estimated horizon is 35.30 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 21.18–49.42 months; its coverage has not been validated.
